title: Writing a CV and Preparing for Interviews
subject: careers

sections.body: A CV/résumé: contact details, a short profile, education, experience (including volunteering and projects), skills, and achievements. Keep it to 1–2 pages and tailor it to each role.
Use action verbs and results: 'Organised a charity bake sale that raised 500.'
Interviews: research the organisation, prepare examples using STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result), practise answers aloud, and prepare 2 questions to ask them.

options: 'Led a team of 4 to build a school app used by 200 students'
hints: Strong lines show action and results.
'Raised 500 for charity by organising a sponsored walk' beats 'Did charity work'.
quiz.explain: It uses an action verb and a measurable result.

quiz.q: What does STAR stand for in interview answers?
hints: It's a structure for telling a story about your experience.
Start with the context, end with the outcome.
Describe where you were, what you needed to do, what you did, and what happened.

quiz.q: At the end of an interview you're asked, 'Do you have any questions for us?' What's the best response?
options: Ask one or two questions you prepared about the role or organisation
Say 'No, I think you've covered everything'
Ask what the organisation actually does
hints: The lesson's interview checklist ends with something you prepare for this exact moment.
Good questions show you've researched the organisation and are genuinely interested in the job.

Worked example: at a university open day, asking 'What do first-year students on this course work on?' shows interest, while asking 'So what subjects do you teach here?' shows you didn't look at the website first.
quiz.explain: The lesson suggests preparing 2 questions to ask. They show interest and research. Having none can seem uninterested, and asking what the organisation does shows you didn't research it.
